connections.user_password_tooltip:
Optional user password
If provided: password will be stored to omnidb configuration's database and used when connecting to this connection.
Leaving blank: No password will be saved and it will be requested to be manually type everytime the user tries to use this connection. If it's a PostgreSQL connection, OmniDB will try to retrieve password from .pgpass.
connections.connection_string_tooltip:
Optional connection string
If provided: OmniDB will use this as the default config, and single inputs for server should not be filled.
If blank: In this case, if this is not a terminal connection, you should instead fill the required single inputs for server above.
connections.ssh_password_tooltip:
Optional ssh password / passphrase
Leave this blank if you dont want the password to be stored.
If provided: OmniDB will use this password when opening a SSH tunnel.
Leaving blank: When the SSH tunnel is requested, OmniDB will prompt an input requesting for this password to be used exclusively to open the connection, but it wont be stored.
connections.ssh_key_tooltip:
Optional ssh key
Leave this blank if you dont want the key to be stored.
If provided: When saving this SSH tunnel, OmniDB will read the content of this file and store just the text, but not the file.

welcome.callout:
We aim to keep OmniDB flexible, secure and work-effective across multiple DBMS.
Just keep in mind that many actions here talk directly to the database you're connected to.
welcome.intro: OmniDB puts you directly in the driver's seat of your databases — that's what makes it so useful. While you're getting comfortable with it, we recommend practicing on a test environment rather than production.

tutorial.main.nav_rail.message:
This is the navigation rail. It gives you access to every section of OmniDB:

  • Welcome, tutorials and useful links.
  • Connections management.
  • Snippets panel.
  • Database (your open connections).

At the bottom you'll also find Getting Started, Settings, and your Account.
tutorial.main.account.message: Clicking the account icon at the bottom of the rail opens this popup: your OmniDB version, username, and a sign-out button.
tutorial.main.account.title: Account
tutorial.utilities_menu.nav_rail.message:
General settings and account management live at the bottom of the navigation rail:

  • Settings (shortcuts, theme, fonts, and -- for superusers -- account/user management).
  • Account (username, version, sign out).

Please, click on the Settings icon.
tutorial.utilities_menu.settings.message:
If you're a superuser, this Settings section has an Account category in the sidebar.

Click on it.
tutorial.utilities_menu.settings.title: Settings
tutorial.utilities_menu.manage_users.mes:
If you just configured OmniDB and logged in with the default admin user, you should create a proper superuser (and later delete the default admin account).

Follow this walkthrough if you want to create other users as well.

Click on Manage Users.
tutorial.utilities_menu.add_user.title: Add a New User
tutorial.utilities_menu.user_options.mes:
• OmniDB login name.
  • OmniDB login password.
  • Defines if the user can manage other OmniDB users.
The default admin user should be deleted once a new super user has been created.
tutorial.connections_menu.nav_rail.messa:
This is the navigation rail. It gives you access to:

  • Connections manager.
  • Welcome, tutorial and useful links.
  • Snippets panel.
  • Your open database connections.

Let's first add a new connection.

Please, click on the Connections icon.
tutorial.connections_menu.title_field.me:
Type a helpful name for the connection.

This is used as name reference on many UI areas.

i.e: Local dvdrental barman.
tutorial.connections_menu.server.message:
Type the server address. Do not include ports.

i.e:127.0.0.1
tutorial.connections_menu.server.title: Server
tutorial.connections_menu.port.message:
Type the port of the server.

i.e: PostgreSQL uses 5432 by default, but if you are using pgbouncer, you may want to use 6432 as the entry point.
tutorial.connections_menu.port.title: Port
tutorial.connections_menu.database.messa:
Type the name of the database.

i.e: postgres, dvdrental.
tutorial.connections_menu.database.title: Database
tutorial.connections_menu.user.message:
Type the name of the user with privileges to access the database.

i.e: postgres.
tutorial.connections_menu.user.title: User
This is optional.

If you don't save the user password, you will be required to manually input it everytime a new connection to this database is started.

If saved, this password will be stored in the database configured for OmniDB (default is omnidb.db).
tutorial.shared.test_connection_message:
You may want to hit 'test' before saving the connection.

After that, click save.
tutorial.terminal_connection.nav_rail.me:
First let's open the connections management interface.

Please, click on the Connections icon in the navigation rail.
tutorial.terminal_connection.title_field:
Type a helpful name for the terminal connection.

This is used as name reference on many UI areas.

i.e: Local terminal.
The terminal utilizes SSH technology.

As you can see, in this case SSH parameters are mandatory.
Type the ssh server address. Do not include ports.

i.e:127.0.0.1
tutorial.terminal_connection.ssh_port.me:
Type the port of the SSH server.

i.e: 22 is a default port for working with SSH tunnels.
tutorial.terminal_connection.ssh_user.me:
Type the name of the SSH user.

i.e: If you are on linux, your linux user is available for a local connection.
tutorial.terminal_connection.ssh_passwor:
If you want you can save the password of your user.

* Leaving this empty will force the tool to request for your password everytime you open a terminal connection.

i.e: If you are on linux, your linux user is available for a local connection.
tutorial.terminal_connection.ssh_key.mes:
This is optional.

It allows you to configure a SSH key.
tutorial.snippets.panel.message:
The snippet panel is now accessible globally, from the navigation rail.

Please, click on the icon.
tutorial.snippets.panel.title: Global Snippet Panel
tutorial.snippets.editor.message:
Inside this tab you can create and edit a snippet.

Go ahead and try to create some simple snippet, i.e:

WHERE true SELECT 1;

Then experiment clicking on the indent button below the editor, and then next.
tutorial.snippets.editor.title: Snippets editor
tutorial.snippets.indent.message:
As you can see, the indentation feature automatically adjusts your code following a pattern.

Now go ahead and click save
tutorial.snippets.indent.title: Indenting
tutorial.snippets.saved.message:
Every snippet you save is stored under your user.

The tree on the left allows you to easily access it by double-clicking on the snippet.
tutorial.snippets.saved.title: Saved Snippets
tutorial.selecting_connection.nav_rail.m:
Your open connections live in the Database section.

Click on the Database icon in the navigation rail.
tutorial.selecting_connection.select.mes:
Open connections are listed here as a strip of tabs, much like browser tabs.

  1. To open a connection, click on the button.
  2. Navigate to the proper technology on the custom menu.
  3. Click on the connection.

Now you can close this walkthrough and open a new connection.
tutorial.connection_tab.current.message: This identifies the database you are connected with:
tutorial.connection_tab.current.title: Current Connection
tutorial.connection_tab.tree.message:
This tree is your main access point to this connection.

How-to:

  • Double-click: expands child nodes based on the database internal structure.
  • Right-click: Context menu with actions based on the node type.
tutorial.connection_tab.tree.title: Aimara Tree
tutorial.connection_tab.properties.messa:
These tabs provide additional info to the node you interact with in the Aimara Tree.

Keep in mind that every node interaction that returns this type of info needs to query for consistency.

To minimize queries, these only run when one of these tabs is visible.

Recommendation: Only open the property/ddl when you need to update this info.
tutorial.connection_tab.properties.title: Properties / DDL
tutorial.connection_tab.inner_tabs.messa:
There are two types of inner_tabs available.

  1. Console Tab: Contains a psql console.
  2. Query Tabs: These have SQL editors whose commands are executed on the selected database.
Keep in mind that when you run a query from the contextual menu of the Aimara Tree, it will open a new query tab and execute it.
tutorial.connection_tab.inner_tabs.title: Inner Tabs
tutorial.connection_tab.actions.message:
These buttons request actions based on the SQL editor and the querying status.

For example, you can run a query, cancel an ongoing query, fetch more, explain, explain analyze.

If you navigate the Tree on the left to find a table and use the action Query Table from it's context menu, the editor will autofill and the run query will be issued.
tutorial.connection_tab.actions.title: Actions Panel
tutorial.connection_tab.result.message:
Query returns will fill the area below your screen, even when they return errors.

After running a query, this area will contain 3 special tabs.

  1. Data: Contains a table with query results, when successful.
  2. Messages: Displays error messages.
  3. Explain: Contains a special component to display explain/explain analyze results.
tutorial.connection_tab.result.title: Query Result
tutorial.getting_started.title: Getting started
